lots.what_it_is: W. Doherty & Co. (Clinton, Ontario, Canada) two-manual parlour reed (pump) organ, walnut-style case with carved fretwork panels and side stop towers, two treadle blow pedals (not a pedal board), with an IHS needlework-topped stool. Probably c.1890-1910.
lots.guide_summary: Nothing survives: researcher gave no entries and my own checks found none. 0 sold, 0 unsold, 0 asking.
lots.working: No SOLD evidence, so keep_max_hammer = 0 and flip_max_hammer = 0. Gowans API re-run for 'organ', 'pump organ', 'reed organ': only organisers and toy lots ('SMALL ORGAN & GUITAR' 20000 cents, listed 2025-10-06, mixed lot, not comparable). WebSearch hit the session cap on my first query, so no further web searching was possible.
lots.confidence_reason: Maker transfer read clearly, but no price evidence of any kind; working action and reeds not seen.
lots.dropped_entries: None to drop (researcher supplied no entries).
lots.key_photo_findings: Enlarged nameboard reads 'Doherty / Clinton Canada' in gilt transfer. Two keyboards visible (two-manual, less common than single-manual parlour organs). Two carpeted blow treadles, no pedal board. Stop knobs in both side towers; right-hand tower knobs look darker and different, possibly couplers or replacements. Case looks clean and recently polished; fretwork intact; mirror/back panel and music desk present. Stool is a separate IHS church needlework stool, not original to the organ.
lots.condition: Case appears good and complete from photos. Mechanical condition (bellows, reeds, keys sounding) unknown.
lots.question_for_armitage: Does it play: do the bellows hold air and do all keys on both manuals sound? Are any stop knobs missing or replaced? Approximate size and weight for removal?
